question.problem: A line $l$ is parallel to $6x-2y=11.$ A possible equation for $l$ is
question.worked_solution:
For two lines to be parallel, they must have the same slope.

To find the slope of the line $6x-2y=11,$ we convert to slope-intercept form:

$$
\begin{aligned}6x-2y & =11 \\ \frac{6}{2}x-\frac{2}{2}y & =\frac{11}{2} \\ 3x-y & =\frac{11}{2} \\ -y & =-3x+\frac{11}{2} \\ y & =3x-\frac{11}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

In slope-intercept form, the slope is the $x$-coefficient. So, the slope is $3.$

From the given options, the only line that has a slope of $3$ is $y=3x-8.$
